highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.156.0 improves platform support and eliminates avoidable native and managed memory overhead.
highlights_body: This update refreshes native build and packaging support across Windows, Apple platforms, Linux, and WebGPU while making image, text, stream, and string handling more efficient and reliable.

bullets.detail: Texture rendering now follows the display refresh cycle, improving the consistency of front-buffered rendering on Android.
Creating SKData from C strings no longer risks reading past the native buffer and writes directly into the managed data object.

bullets.lead: Image pixel copies use less managed overhead
bullets.detail: Managed image pixel-copy operations avoid unnecessary work, reducing overhead when moving pixel data.

bullets.lead: Text and stream handling retain fewer native resources
bullets.detail: Feature-string decoding avoids a native allocation, HarfBuzz UTF-32 conversion reuses buffers, and front-buffered streams no longer retain resources unnecessarily.
Apple targets now use newer deployment minimums; verify that applications target supported OS versions before updating.

bullets.lead: Native packages updated across Windows, Linux, and WebGPU
bullets.detail: Windows native and ANGLE builds use the modern Visual Studio toolchain, Linux resolves bundled HarfBuzz functions locally, and the WebGPU implementation is included in libSkiaSharp.a.

contributor_summaries.VirgilMing: Bundled Linux HarfBuzz linkage and Blazor CPU sample test stabilization
